title: Bitcoin AI Model Review — Week 36: 3 of 6 Calls Correct
meta_description: Week 36 graded: 3 of 6 Bitcoin calls correct (50%). All-time: 53.1% over 32 public calls. Paper portfolio +11.9% vs holding.

intro: For the week spanning 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-05, the model finished with 3 correct calls out of 6 resolved signals, yielding an accuracy rate of 50.0 percent.
Performance was split down the middle, ending on a 2 hit streak on Friday and Saturday after major high-confidence missteps mid-week.
We publish every result plainly because holding our predictive system accountable requires total transparency.
days: The model opened Monday with a HOLD call at 50.6 percent confidence, which graded as incorrect when price dropped 2.16 percent.
It rebounded on Tuesday with another HOLD signal at 47.2 percent confidence, correctly catching a minor decline of 0.53 percent.
Following a severe misstep on Wednesday that we will break down in our spotlight, Thursday brought a BUY signal at 74 percent confidence that failed when price fell 2.26 percent.
The week closed on Friday and Saturday with consecutive HOLD signals at 41.1 percent and 41.8 percent confidence, both grading as hits with identical flat price moves of 0.09 percent.
spotlight: The worst call of the week occurred on Wednesday, 2026-09-02, when the model issued a SELL signal with high confidence of 81.5 percent.
Instead of dropping, the market rallied aggressively, posting a sharp price gain of 4.87 percent.
This call was flatly wrong, grading as a clear miss for our highest confidence signal of the period.
trend: Price action across the six days was volatile, featuring steep drops early and mid-week alongside a strong mid-week surge.
The model struggled to track directional momentum, missing both major directional swings while picking up hits only during quiet sideways action.
portfolio: Starting with 10000.0 dollars over 33 days, the model portfolio ended at 11193.74 dollars, representing a return of 11.94 percent after accounting for 6 trades and 95.24 dollars in paid fees.
Over that same timeframe, a simple buy and hold benchmark reached 12329.01 dollars for a return of 23.29 percent.
That leaves the active strategy at negative 11.35 percent relative to hold, confirming that following the calls performed worse than simply holding.
record: All time, the model stands at 17 hits and 15 misses across 32 resolved calls, which translates to an overall accuracy rate of 53.1 percent.
This week's 50.0 percent accuracy sat slightly below that baseline, while the 29 resolved calls in the recent evaluation window reflect a 55.2 percent accuracy rate.
With only 32 total resolved calls logged so far, this sample size remains far too small to establish definitive conclusions.

research.title: Why the model predicts regimes, not prices
paragraphs: The model does not predict prices. It classifies the next twenty four hours into an upward, downward, or flat regime.
Exact price targets are noise at this horizon. Regimes are the part of the problem a model can actually learn.
Ask a model for a number it cannot know and it will hand you one anyway. We would rather ask it a question it can answer.
